waves.name: Batch utility jobs and platform readiness
waves.rationale: Six jobs that run no application program and touch no dataset another entry point uses: the CICS system definition load, two IDCAMS definers, an FTP demo, a catalog listing and RACF commands. Sound as a wave only as a toolchain and pipeline proof; most of it is replaced by platform configuration, not ported. CREADB2 left this wave for wave 7 (deviation 1).
waves.unblocks: Nothing in the tree calls these jobs. It is a chore wave. Its value is a proven build, deploy, rollback and diff pipeline and a first decision on the normalization spec before real programs move.

waves.name: Read-only batch over the masters
waves.rationale: Four programs that print or convert the account, card, xref and customer masters, and the importer of the branch export. They write nothing another entry point reads, so they can be deployed, diffed and rolled back independently. Their input layouts (CVACT01Y, CVACT02Y, CVACT03Y, CVCUS01Y) are the ones the later waves must read. CBIMPORT has one output DD that no JCL maps, and CBACT01C calls an assembler routine the extractor did not read.
waves.unblocks: Proves that zoned decimal and sign overpunch in the master files are read correctly, and produces the first replay captures of the masters that waves 3, 5 and 6 depend on.

waves.name: Sign-on, menus and read-only online views
waves.rationale: Online programs that write nothing another entry point uses: sign-on, the two menus, account view, card view and the two transaction views. Sign-on, COMEN01C and COADM01C form one call cycle, and COTRN00C and COTRN01C form another, so each moves whole. The menus dispatch through the tables in app/cpy/COMEN02Y.cpy and app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy, which bounds the computed calls to the programs of waves 3, 5, 6 and 7. This wave is the front door: it must route to legacy programs of later waves until they move. Confidence stays below high because six of the seven units make computed calls.
waves.unblocks: The router that every later online wave switches behind, and the read paths for account, card and transaction data.

waves.name: Build tooling, GDG bases and demo jobs
waves.rationale: Batch jobs that read datasets through a utility: three compile jobs, one GDG definer, two internal reader demos and three build procs. None runs a business program. TXT2PDF1 left this wave for wave 5 (deviation 3) and IMSMQCMP left for wave 7 (deviation 2). The wave is retained because the extractor placed it, but it is mostly do_not_port.
waves.unblocks: Nothing. It is a chore wave, and the honest plan is to replace it with the target build pipeline and delete it.

waves.name: The nightly batch cycle: posting, master refresh, interest, report, statements
waves.rationale: Every batch job that reloads or appends to a shared master or to a GDG the cycle shares, with the three must-not-break items in it: daily posting (POSTTRAN and CBTRN02C), the account and card master refresh (ACCTFILE and CARDFILE), and the transaction report (TRANREPT, CBTRN03C, CORPT00C). It is 56 units, and I did not cut it. TRANREPT writes TRANSACT.BKUP(+1), the generation COMBTRAN reads as (0), so the report is not independent of posting (app/jcl/TRANREPT.jcl:33, app/jcl/COMBTRAN.jcl:24). The wrapper scripts and Control-M folders chain the same jobs. Port order inside the wave is in 03-waves.md. The wave shares ACCTDATA and TRANSACT with the online writers of wave 6, so the data owner stays the legacy VSAM through wave 6.
waves.unblocks: Wave 6. Online writers can move only after one owner is chosen for the account and transaction masters, and this wave defines how they are rebuilt each night.

waves.name: Online writers of the account, card, transaction and user masters
waves.rationale: Nine online programs that write a master another entry point also uses: account update, card update, bill payment, transaction add, and the four user programs. Eight contract edges run from these programs to wave 5 programs and five run back, so the two waves are bound by data even though the code is separate. Every unit makes computed calls, bounded by the menu tables and the COMMAREA return pattern.
waves.unblocks: Retirement of the CICS files and of the CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL dance in the nightly cycle.

waves.name: Authorization, IMS, DB2 and MQ subsystem
waves.rationale: Everything that touches DB2, IMS or MQ, plus two jobs moved here by deviations 1 and 2. It holds the real time card authorization decision program. The IMS DBD and PSB files, the DB2 DDL and DCLGEN files and the .ctl members are not parsed, MQ is not modeled, and four of its units make computed calls, so confidence is low and the wave should be re-assessed once those files are read.
waves.unblocks: Decommissioning of IMS, DB2 and MQ on the mainframe. Nothing else in the tree waits on it, except that CA-7 chains POSTTRAN after CBPAUP0J in this wave.

unassigned.reason: Not reached by any static edge, no JCL step in the tree runs it, and 28 computed calls could target it. It reads only and posts nothing. Confirm with the client whether it is a retired verification copy of CBTRN02C before placing it.

deviations.reason: The extractor could not see DB2. The job runs IKJEFT01 with SYSTSIN members that live in .ctl files the extractor lists as not parsed. Those members run DSN and DSNTIAD and create CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE, so it belongs with the DB2 subsystem wave.

The extractor saw only the libraries this compile job reads, not what it builds. PARM CICS,DLI,COBOL3 and the MQ copy library show it compiles an IMS and MQ program, so it belongs with the IMS, DB2 and MQ wave. It is build tooling and is also listed in do_not_port.

The CA-7 listing, which the extractor lists as not parsed, triggers TXT2PDF1 from CREASTMT. It reads STATEMNT.PS, which CBSTM03A writes. risks.json scores it high-high (a REXX library outside the tree, customer statements), so it must not lead the wave that produces its input.
